review_note: Pinned lemma 87 says every geometric base-change multiplicity is 1 or a power of characteristic p; Stage A unpacks characteristic zero to 1 and characteristic p to p^n. The two cases are equivalent, including n=0.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-multiplicities-field-extension}
Let $K/k$ be a field extension. Let $Z$ be an integral locally algebraic
scheme over $k$. The multiplicity $m_{Z', Z_K}$ of an irreducible
component $Z' \subset Z_K$ is $1$ or a power of the characteristic of $k$.
statement:
Let $K/k$ be a field extension. Let $Z$ be an integral locally algebraic
scheme over $k$. The multiplicity $m_{Z', Z_K}$ of an irreducible
component $Z' \subset Z_K$ is $1$ when $\operatorname{char}(k)=0$, and is a power of $p$ when $\operatorname{char}(k)=p>0$.
hypotheses:
Let $K/k$ be a field extension. Let $Z$ be an integral locally algebraic
scheme over $k$.
conclusions:
The multiplicity $m_{Z', Z_K}$ of an irreducible
component $Z' \subset Z_K$ is $1$ or a power of the characteristic of $k$.

review_note: Pinned lemma 146 assumes positive characteristic p, perfect closure k^perf, algebraic X/k and r≥0, concluding cokernel of injective r-cycle base-change map is p-POWER torsion. The draft retains injectivity and the torsion type.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-how-different}
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$ with perfect closure $k^{perf}$.
Let $X$ be an algebraic scheme over $k$. Let $r \geq 0$ be an integer.
The cokernel of the injective map $Z_r(X) \to Z_r(X_{k^{perf}})$ is a
$p$-power torsion module (More on Algebra, Definition
\ref{more-algebra-definition-f-power-torsion}).
